clue.text: Protest by class, a convincing demonstration

parts.note: to object is to protest
a class is a lesson at school

explanation.surface: A pupil complains about the class, and it turns into a persuasive display.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example that teaches a point vividly, which is a convincing demonstration.

clue.text: Rings circling the lines in play

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the rings enclose the other letters

parts.note: O, a ring shape, twice gives rings
L is line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Stage rings surround the actors delivering their lines in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' signals that the two rings sit at either end, one opening and one closing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Shakespeare tragedy about the Moor of Venice, an example of a play.

clue.text: Caretaker of a joint in resort overlooking river

indicators.note: overlooking means sitting above, so in this down clue the shuffled letters come before the next piece
to resort something is to sort it again, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A caretaker at a joint in a holiday resort beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' rearranges A JOINT into JANITO; 'overlooking' puts it above R.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building, cleaning and maintaining it, which is a caretaker's job.

clue.text: Dull, sitcom involving the French head of state

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the sitcom's name wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Cheers is the American sitcom set in a Boston bar
le is French for the

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of state is used

explanation.surface: A dull sitcom that features the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheers was a long-running American sitcom; 'involving' opens it before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheerless lacks brightness or joy, so it is dreary and dull.

clue.text: Large old vessel, a muted green

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids

explanation.surface: An old, large container painted a soft shade of green.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a soft greyish-green, the shade of many Scottish tweeds.

clue.text: Spot occupied by male, adult showing endurance

indicators.note: occupied by means having something inside, so the spot holds the next piece

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A place taken by a grown man who shows staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental strength to keep going, which is endurance.

clue.text: Work with Universal, fast becoming rich

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
U is the British film classification for universal
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Working with Universal Studios quickly makes someone wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavish and wealthy, so it is a synonym for rich.

clue.text: Naval man? Fit type force employed

indicators.note: employed means put to use, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sailor is described as a fit sort who has joined the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty officer is a non-commissioned rank in the navy, so is one example of a naval man.

clue.text: Hence broadcast about a new lift

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the next pieces
broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters of the word are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A statement that a broadcast about something new gave someone a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' shuffles HENCE into ENHCE, and 'about' wraps that round A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise or improve it, so lift is a synonym.

clue.text: American four, returning, reportedly steered clear of bridge

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for steered clear of is taken by its sound

parts.note: to duck something is to dodge it, so steered clear of means ducked

explanation.surface: Four Americans heading home avoided a bridge, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the whole of American four; 'reportedly' marks a sound-alike for the past tense of duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway over a valley, a particular kind of bridge.

clue.text: Runs inside to take care of dogs, leaders of the pack?

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the runs go into the next word

parts.note: to tend is to take care of
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
setters are breeds of gun dog

explanation.surface: A dog walker runs indoors to look after the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: With dogs in the clue, 'leaders of the pack' suggests lead dogs; it means people who start fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendsetters lead fashion and others follow, so they are cryptically the leaders of the pack.

clue.text: Satellite town initially associated with the Spanish celebrity

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of town is used

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A town linked to a famous Spanish figure becomes a satellite of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the famous 1962 communications satellite that relayed the first live transatlantic television.

clue.text: Anger shown during term at sea in galley

indicators.note: shown during means appearing in the middle of, so the word for anger sits inside the other letters
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of term get jumbled

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Fury breaks out among the crew of a galley during a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the nautical surface but is the anagram signal; 'shown during' places the anger within the shuffled TRME.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient warship rowed by three banks of oars, so it is a type of galley.

clue.text: Smell nothing grim

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing
dour means stern or grim

explanation.surface: A bleak, dour smell, or rather a smell that is no grim thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell; the two words are simple synonyms.

clue.text: Film: 'Spellbound'?

definitions.meaning: A 2007 Disney film mixing animation and live action
spellbound means bewitched, held under a spell

explanation.surface: A cinema listing: the film Spellbound, with a question mark hinting at another title.
explanation.walkthrough: Spellbound is itself a Hitchcock film, which tempts solvers to read the whole clue as one title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held by magic is enchanted, the same sense as spellbound; Enchanted is also a film title.

clue.text: Agreement to include wayward son in survey

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the survey wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a census is an official survey of a population

indicators.note: wayward means straying, so the letters of son go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: An agreement to count a disobedient son in a population survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges the boy into ONS; 'to include' opens the survey right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general agreement among a group.

clue.text: Lodger, perhaps unattached, meets mother with child

parts.note: someone unattached is free, single
ma is mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A single lodger moves in with a mother and her child.
explanation.walkthrough: A Freemason belongs to a Masonic lodge, so 'Lodger' is a member of a lodge, not a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so a member is cryptically a lodger; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: What map line may show, a route winding across Quebec

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the shuffled letters lie on either side of the next piece
winding means twisting, so the letters of the phrase are bent into a new order

parts.note: Quebec is the NATO alphabet word for Q

explanation.surface: A map might show a winding road across the Canadian province of Quebec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges A ROUTE into EUATOR; 'across' splits it round Q.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary line round the Earth's middle drawn on maps and globes.

clue.text: A disfigurement concealed by the old lady's cosmetic

indicators.note: concealed by means hidden inside, so the earlier pieces sit within the last

parts.note: the old lady is slang for mother, so ma; the possessive is surface only
a scar is a disfigurement

explanation.surface: Mum's make-up hides a blemish on her face.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic applied to darken and thicken eyelashes.

clue.text: Colour of line round centre of Earth

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: the oche is the line behind which darts players stand to throw

indicators.note: centre of means the middle letter of the word Earth is taken

explanation.surface: Asking what colour the line around the middle of the Earth would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the equator; the line is really the oche of darts, wrapped round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment, so it is a named colour.

clue.text: Arrive after published result

indicators.note: after means following, so the word for arrive goes at the end

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: The result arrives after it has been published.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the consequence of something, a synonym for result.

clue.text: Personally involved with worker — occasionally swoon!

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand or deckhand

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so alternate letters of swoon are kept

explanation.surface: Someone personally involved with a worker swoons now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps the first, third and fifth letters of swoon, giving SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on manager takes a direct, practical part in the work rather than delegating.

clue.text: Warship seen from coast, heading for Rosyth

parts.note: to cruise is to coast along at an easy steady speed

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of Rosyth is taken

explanation.surface: A warship is spotted off the coast, making for the naval base at Rosyth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosyth is a Scottish naval dockyard on the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, medium-sized class of warship.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife make a fresh start

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A French husband and his wife decide to begin again.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to begin again or restart, so it means making a fresh start.

clue.text: Wiped out text, start to finish, describing elected Conservative

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line round, so the first piece encloses the second
start to finish means the first letter is moved round to the end of the word

parts.note: someone elected is in office, so elected gives in

explanation.surface: A text is erased, the whole message, about a Conservative who won a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' sends the first letter to the end, giving EXTT; 'describing' wraps that round the elected Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that is extinct has died out completely, so it has been wiped out.

clue.text: Learn a new skill on set

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a train is a connected series or set, as in a train of events

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick up a fresh skill while working on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to be trained again, acquiring a different skill or profession.

clue.text: Godparent playing spoons right at the back

indicators.note: at the back means the next piece goes after the shuffled letters
playing suggests the letters are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A godparent sits at the back of the room playing the spoons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' fits a musician but shuffles the fodder; 'at the back' puts the right after it.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism a sponsor is the person who stands surety for the child, another word for godparent.

clue.text: Railway in splendid cowboy film

parts.note: great means splendid
a western is a cowboy film

explanation.surface: A fine cowboy film set on a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Western Railway was a historic British railway company running from London to the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Western is the name of a famous British railway company.
